name: indahl-data
description: Measurements of published claims against the data behind them, from indahl.ai: the calibration IBM publishes for its quantum processors checked against our own runs, and checks on the papers, statistics, quotations, citations, packages and models a person brings. Every answer names its source and when it was read, with the outcome ABOVE, BELOW, CONSISTENT or CANNOT_TELL relative to what was stated. Read-only.

interface.longDescription: Measurements of published claims against the data behind them, from indahl.ai: the calibration IBM publishes for its quantum processors checked against our own runs, and checks on the papers, statistics, quotations, citations, packages and models a person brings. Every answer names its source and when it was read, with the outcome ABOVE, BELOW, CONSISTENT or CANNOT_TELL relative to what was stated. Read-only.
defaultPrompt: Does this Hugging Face model match its license file?
Has this paper been corrected or withdrawn? (DOI or arXiv id)

positive.description: Check IBM Quantum calibration before a run.
positive.prompt: I am about to run a circuit on ibm_kingston using qubits 0, 1, 2, 3 and 4. Is IBM's published calibration for those qubits fit to rely on, and which qubits look better?
positive.expected_behavior: Reads the newest calibration record IBM published for ibm_kingston, applies the QIA package rules to qubits 0 to 4 (stale figures, T2 above twice T1, T1 and T2 measured far apart, zero error figures), states the record's age, and lists unflagged qubits with the lowest readout error.

positive.description: Check one paper for retractions and corrections.
positive.prompt: Has this paper been retracted or corrected? 10.1016/S0140-6736(97)11096-0
positive.expected_behavior: Reads the Crossref record and finds the 2004 correction and the 2010 retraction notices with their DOIs and dates.

positive.description: Recompute reported statistics from their own numbers.
positive.prompt: Check the statistics in this passage: "Participants in the treatment group scored higher, t(28) = 2.20, p = .01, and the effect held at follow-up, F(1, 40) = 4.10, p = .049."
positive.expected_behavior: Recomputes both tests: t(28) = 2.20 gives p of about .036, so the stated p = .01 reads BELOW; F(1, 40) = 4.10 gives p of about .0496, CONSISTENT with .049.

positive.description: Check a quotation against its source.
positive.prompt: Is this quote accurate? "deep learning allows computational models that are composed of multiple processing layers to learn representations of data" Source: https://www.nature.com/articles/nature14539
positive.expected_behavior: Reads the named page and marks the quotation VERBATIM, ALTERED (with the source's exact words and the differences), NOT_FOUND or CANNOT_TELL; here VERBATIM, with where it sits in the page.

positive.description: Read an interval as one of four outcomes.
positive.prompt: Our trial found a difference of 1.8 points, 95% interval 0.2 to 3.4. The smallest difference that matters clinically is 2 points. Can we say the treatment works?
positive.expected_behavior: Tests both alternatives: the interval excludes zero but still reaches 2 points and beyond, so the answer on the question that matters is CANNOT_TELL, with the width needed to decide.

negative.expected_behavior: The app should not be invoked because the request is outside indahl.ai's published measurements.
